# Repository checks

Four GitHub Actions checks are required for pull requests to `main`. The
existing **Private development validation** workflow is retained unchanged;
its name identifies the inherited workflow, not permission to use private
datasets. A separate maintenance workflow adds README and JSON checks.

| Required check | Scope | Limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **validate (ubuntu-latest)** | Python 3.11 workspace preparation verification and synthetic unit tests on Ubuntu. | Does not run final-paper-required mode or grant publication or operational permission. |
| **validate (windows-latest)** | The same retained preparation checks and synthetic tests on Windows. | A platform-capability skip remains a skip; results apply to the tested environment and selection. |
| **README links** | Local Markdown links and images in tracked Markdown files whose names contain `README`, ignoring letter case. Checks tracked targets, exact filename case, repository boundaries and Markdown heading or explicit HTML anchors. | Does not test external websites, bare URLs, paths shown as code, links in other documents, or citations inside PDFs and Word files. |
| **JSON syntax** | Every tracked `.json` and `.jsonl` file, ignoring extension case. Checks UTF-8 encoding, strict JSON syntax, unique object keys and rejection of `NaN` and `Infinity`. JSONL requires one complete JSON value per line. | Does not validate schemas, data quality, governance meaning, signatures or provenance. JSON inside ZIP archives is not extracted. |

## Retained development validation

The existing workflow installs the pinned dependencies from
`requirements-release.txt`, runs `tools/verify_private_workspace.py` without
`--require-final-papers`, and runs `tests/unit/` with synthetic fixtures. The
workspace checker examines source selection, historical-copy identities,
standards hashes, syntax, selected schemas and registered document identities
within its documented scope.

Preparation mode permits an empty paper allowlist during owner conversion.
A preparation PASS therefore does not establish readiness to seal. The separate
`--require-final-papers` mode checks the registered two-PDF selection; it still
does not establish visual quality, legal rights or publication permission.
See [Local Standards Checks](../docs/execution/LOCAL_CHECKS.md).

Unit tests use synthetic fixtures and temporary keys. They do not issue real
authorization, train a model or modify historical evidence. Any new run has its
own observed outcomes; do not copy earlier totals into its report.

## Maintenance check coverage

The maintenance workflow runs on every pull request to `main`, every push to
`main`, and manual workflow runs, without path filters. Its checks read files
without rewriting them or running the three-path pipelines.

The README check runs offline. It handles inline and reference Markdown links,
images, angle-bracket paths containing spaces and HTML links. External URL
schemes are excluded. Fragment checking applies to Markdown destinations;
PDF fragment syntax is outside this check. The initial baseline is 110 local
links across 54 README files, with one external link skipped. References outside
this scope still require manual review.

The initial syntax baseline is 182 JSON files and no JSONL files. Future
tracked JSONL files are checked automatically. UTF-8 byte-order marks, empty
JSONL files and blank JSONL record lines are rejected. LF and CRLF line endings
and a single optional final newline are supported. There are no historical
syntax exceptions in this repository. Counts describe the starting point,
not a fixed required inventory.

These checks do not rebuild manifests or packages, download models, run GPU
training or generate CSC evidence. Original papers, artifacts and published
release assets retain their identities.

## Run locally

Run from the repository root in the appropriate Python environment. Keep
generated bytecode out of this repository by using `-B` as shown.

For the retained development checks, use Python 3.11:

```sh
python -m pip install -r requirements-release.txt
python -B tools/verify_private_workspace.py
python -B -m unittest discover -s tests/unit -p "test_*.py" -v
```

For the additional maintenance checks, use Python 3.12:

```sh
python -m pip install --require-hashes -r .github/ci/requirements.txt
python -B -m unittest discover -s .github/ci/tests -v
python -B .github/ci/check_readme_links.py --root .
python -B .github/ci/check_json.py --root .
```

The maintenance checkers examine only Git-tracked paths. Stage intended new
files before checking their links locally so the inventory matches CI. Pass
`--root .` explicitly when invoking either maintenance checker from the root.
All required checks must still pass on the pull request.

For the separate paper-presence and identity check, use Python 3.11:

```sh
python -B tools/verify_private_workspace.py --require-final-papers
```

This last command is not part of the unchanged development workflow and is not
a publication gate by itself. Follow the full local standards guidance rather
than treating a successful command as authority to publish.

## Merge requirements and workflow permissions

The `main` protection requires all four named checks and an up-to-date proposed
branch. Human diff review and conversation resolution remain part of the
[contribution workflow](../CONTRIBUTING.md). If a required job is renamed or
removed, coordinate its workflow and protection settings so merging is not
blocked waiting for a check that no longer runs.

Both workflows use read-only repository tokens, pinned actions, no persisted
checkout credentials and no repository secrets. Pull-request checks use
`pull_request`, not `pull_request_target`. GitHub may require maintainer approval
before a first-time external contributor's workflow runs. The maintenance
parser dependencies are pinned with hashes; the retained development workflow
continues to use its existing version-pinned dependency file.

Tests under `.github/ci/tests/` exercise the maintenance helpers. They supplement
the retained `tests/unit/` suite and do not replace it. Passing CI is bounded
technical evidence, not independent assurance, legal approval, governance
authority or production permission.
